security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 84 static findings in SKILL.md and references/component-index.md. The findings are false positives caused by markdown inline code, TSX examples, CSS class names, file paths, and responsive grid guidance. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, command execution intent, or malicious instructions were found.

content.value_statement: Paperclip UI work can drift when components, tokens, and layouts are created ad hoc. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a shared design guide for consistent frontend implementation.
actual_capabilities: Documents Paperclip design principles, React stack choices, and Tailwind token usage.
Defines typography, radius, shadow, color, status, and priority conventions.
Explains when to create reusable components and when to use direct Tailwind classes.
Provides composition patterns for rows, lists, property panels, metrics, progress bars, comments, tables, and logs.
Describes the app layout, design guide page rules, file naming conventions, and component index maintenance.
Lists available UI primitives, custom components, layout components, form components, utilities, and hooks.
limitations: Guidance is specific to Paperclip and its React, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, and Radix stack.
The skill does not execute tests, inspect the live app, or enforce design rules automatically.
The component inventory can become stale if authors do not update the reference file.
It expects separate frontend quality and web best practice skills for broader review.

use_cases.title: Create a New Component
use_cases.description: Use the guide to choose tokens, variants, file names, states, and design guide examples for a new Paperclip component.

use_cases.title: Review UI Consistency
use_cases.description: Compare a page or feature against Paperclip typography, layout, status, priority, and interaction patterns.

use_cases.title: Document Component Changes
use_cases.description: Update the component index and design guide page when a reusable UI pattern changes or expands.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Component Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the design-guide skill to review my plan for a new Paperclip component. Check tokens, typography, variants, file placement, and design guide updates.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reusable Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the design-guide skill to implement this Paperclip component. Follow existing shadcn/ui composition, CVA variants, cn usage, status conventions, and file naming rules.

prompt_templates.title: Align a Page Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the design-guide skill to refactor this Paperclip page layout. Align it with the sidebar, breadcrumb, main content, properties panel, spacing, and responsive patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex UI Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the design-guide skill to audit this UI change for design system drift. Identify duplicated patterns, missing documentation, inconsistent tokens, weak states, and component reuse opportunities.

output_examples.input: Review a new issue row component for Paperclip.
output_examples.output: The response identifies EntityRow as the right base pattern, requires StatusIcon before PriorityIcon, and recommends StatusBadge in the trailing slot.

output_examples.input: Plan dashboard metric cards for an agents page.
output_examples.output: The response recommends MetricCard in a responsive four-column grid, with semantic tokens, small shadows, and established typography for values and labels.

output_examples.input: Update the design guide after adding a reusable selector.
output_examples.output: The response lists the design guide section to add, variants to show, interactive states to include, and component index fields to update.

best_practices: Start with existing primitives and custom composites before creating a new component.
Use semantic tokens, established typography, and shared status or priority components.
Update both the design guide page and component index when reusable UI changes.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode raw colors, custom type scales, or one-off status styling.
Do not modify shadcn/ui primitives directly when composition can extend them.
Do not add reusable components without examples, states, variants, and reference documentation.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Paperclip frontend components and pages that follow the project design system.

faq.question: Which stack does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui, Radix UI, Lucide React, and CVA.

faq.question: Does it replace visual design review?
faq.answer: No. It provides Paperclip-specific rules and expects broader frontend quality review from companion design skills.

faq.question: Can it create new components?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to create components, where to place files, and how to document variants and states.

faq.question: Does it include a component inventory?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference file lists primitives, custom components, layout components, form components, utilities, and hooks.

faq.question: Is it safe to use?
faq.answer: The reviewed files contain documentation and illustrative TSX snippets. No malicious instructions or execution behavior were found.
